freshReview.attemptedCounterexample: Actually challenged the formal botanical-family target rather than the inverse ginger/turmeric membership question0976. Both newly reopened bodies support Zingiberaceae: Britannica names the ginger family and discusses turmeric/common ginger as economic members; Wikipedia explicitly includes turmeric, with selected Curcuma/Kew and Zingiber/Kew references rather than paired Britannica. Brassicaceae (mustard), Fabaceae (fenugreek/legumes) and Iridaceae (saffron/irises) are real same-rank botanical families and none contains common culinary ginger/turmeric. The separate Zingiber officinale fun fact is directly named in both actual contextual passages; wild ginger Asarum and other vernacular gingers are excluded by common culinary wording. Final ordered choices read individually; correct fourth option remains unique.
